clue.text: The Spanish father tucking into fat (not round) cheese

indicators.note: something tucking into food goes inside it, so these letters sit within the other word
'not' tells us to take away the thing named next from the word before it

parts.note: obese means very fat
O is round in shape
el is Spanish for 'the'
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A Spanish dad tucks into some rich, fatty cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' is not a shape description but the letter O, which is removed from the word for fat before the Spanish article and father go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bel Paese is a mild, soft Italian cheese, so it is an example of a cheese.

clue.text: Bewilder male, American, during social gathering

indicators.note: during means within the span of something, so these letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: a bee is a social gathering for shared work, as in a quilting bee
M is the abbreviation for male
US stands for the United States, so American
the end of the word for a work party

explanation.surface: An American man at a party leaves everyone baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: BEE splits to hold M and US. A bee is a gathering of neighbours for a joint task or contest, as in a spelling bee.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse someone is to puzzle or confuse them, a synonym for bewilder.

clue.text: Biblical character, with another, beheaded sea monster

indicators.note: a beheaded word has lost its head, meaning its first letter

parts.note: Levi is a son of Jacob in Genesis
Nathan is another Old Testament figure, the prophet who rebuked David

explanation.surface: A biblical figure and his companion were beheaded by a sea monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another biblical character; losing its first letter, NATHAN becomes ATHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is a huge sea creature described in the Book of Job and the Psalms.

clue.text: Is surrounded by beer in passageway

indicators.note: surrounded by means enclosed, so the first word sits inside the second

parts.note: ale is a type of beer; it opens here
taken as written
the rest of the beer

explanation.surface: Someone is surrounded by beer in a corridor, perhaps at a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves, so a kind of passage.

clue.text: Pupils translated old chronicles about Hungary's capital

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the words wrap around the extra letter
translated text is turned into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed

indicators.note: a capital letter here means the first letter of the place named

parts.note: the first letter of Hungary

explanation.surface: Students translating ancient chronicles about the Hungarian capital, Budapest.
explanation.walkthrough: Hungary's capital looks like Budapest, but it is the letter that heads the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils are children attending school, so the two terms are synonyms.

clue.text: Port and rum does it

indicators.note: rum here means odd or strange, so the following word is put into a strange order

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Two drinks, port and rum, seem to be doing the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Port and rum look like a pair of drinks, but port is the definition and rum the signal to rearrange. 'It' for SA is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port city in Ukraine, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Policeman and soldier, crossing top of Alps, go missing

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the soldier's letters lie on either side of the single letter

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
a sapper is an army engineer; most of the word comes here

indicators.note: the top of a word written downward is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Alps
the last letter of the engineer

explanation.surface: A police officer and a soldier crossing over a mountain peak vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: SAPPER, a British term for a military engineer, opens up to take the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to vanish or cease to be seen, the same as going missing.

clue.text: Team going round second of cliffs, slip

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the team word surrounds the single letter

parts.note: a side is a team; it opens here

indicators.note: 'second of' picks out the letter in position two of the following word

parts.note: the second letter of cliffs
the rest of the team word

explanation.surface: A mountain-rescue team circling a cliff edge loses its footing.
explanation.definitionFit: To slide is to slip or skid, as on ice; the two verbs are near synonyms.

clue.text: Stair repaired with effort and skill

indicators.note: something repaired has been taken apart and put back together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
a try is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: A staircase mended with hard work and craftsmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill or craftsmanship, so the two nouns are close synonyms.

clue.text: Film king in kitchen where paintings are on show

indicators.note: 'in' places the royal letter inside the word for the kitchen

parts.note: a picture is a film, as in 'going to the pictures'
a galley is a kitchen on a ship or plane; most of it comes here
R is short for rex, Latin for king
the last letter of the ship's kitchen

explanation.surface: A movie about a king in his kitchen, set where art is displayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery for pictures is a room or building in which works of art are exhibited.

clue.text: Girl with mother is about five

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the word before wraps around the number that follows

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little girl with her mum is nearly five years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'approximately five' in the surface reading; in the wordplay it puts the Roman numeral inside the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mavis is a female first name, and crosswords often define given names simply as a girl or boy.

clue.text: One wearing rough one? Right article for an ascetic

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: a garment that is rough on the one wearing it
second meaning: the fitting garment for someone practising self-denial

explanation.surface: Someone asks what rough garment a hermit should wear, and is told the right one for a self-denier.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads like it describes a person; 'one' is in fact the garment itself, rough on its wearer. It is woven from goat or horse hair and worn next to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious ascetics wore this scratchy garment as self-mortification, so it is the classic clothing item of penance.

clue.text: Aunt Sally, the last to fuss about two animals

indicators.note: 'the last to' points at the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of fuss
C is short for circa, Latin for about
two creatures side by side: a primate and a horned farm animal

explanation.surface: An aunt called Sally is the last person to make a fuss over a couple of pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two animals' supplies two separate words. An Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing things at a dummy, and so a figure set up to be attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms describe someone made the target of blame or criticism, often unfairly, for others' failings.

clue.text: Crowd of journalists

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to crowd or push in on someone
second meaning: reporters and newspapers collectively

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single phrase for a pack of reporters; split it at 'of' and each half is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to throng or push close as a verb and also names the news media as a collective noun.

clue.text: Rough strip search involving writer and board member?

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one word is included among the other letters
rough suggests something roughed up and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A rough strip search of a novelist who sits on a company's board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board member' suggests a company director; here it is someone who works with the wooden boards of a vessel, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The crew member responsible for woodwork on a sailing vessel works the planks of the deck, so is whimsically a member of the board.

clue.text: Ask parent about Russian writer

indicators.note: 'about' can mean turned around and around, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: Ask your mother or father about a writer from Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it introduces the topic of the question; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Pasternak was the Russian poet and novelist who wrote Doctor Zhivago.

clue.text: Beastly Great Dane in open-air restaurant

indicators.note: beastly means nasty or wild, so the letters are treated roughly and disordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: A badly behaved large dog causing havoc at an outdoor café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' seems to describe the dog, which is apt for a Great Dane, but it is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor area where tea and light refreshments are served, so an open-air café.

clue.text: Endless thought follows incident in the latter part of the day

definitions.text: the latter part of the day

indicators.note: endless means losing its final letter
follows means this piece comes after the next one in order

parts.note: an event is an incident or occurrence
an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: Endless reflection after an incident late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' puts the shortened thought after the incident, so the order of the pieces is the reverse of the clue's.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, which is the later part of the day.

clue.text: Cosmetic applied by Wells's scientist?

parts.note: surface reading: a face cream used by a scientist in an H. G. Wells story
setter's reading: Wells's Invisible Man was a scientist who made himself disappear, so his cream would make him vanish

explanation.surface: A beauty product used by a scientist in an H. G. Wells novel.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Invisible Man, the scientist Griffin makes himself unseen; the joke is that a real skin cream with a disappearing name would be his choice.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a real type of light moisturiser that seems to be absorbed into the skin, so it is a cosmetic.

clue.text: One may suit you

parts.note: surface reading: something that might be suitable or agreeable to you
setter's reading: suit is a verb meaning to fit you out with a suit of clothes

explanation.surface: Something or someone that may be just right for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' reads as 'be suitable for', but the setter means making you a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor is the craftsman who makes made-to-measure clothes such as jackets and trousers.

clue.text: Language used by beginner in ring breaking hooter

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the letter goes within the other word

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose; its first part opens the word

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of ring
the rest of the slang word for the nose

explanation.surface: A language spoken by a beginner whose ring has broken a car horn.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter is British slang for a nose, here NOSE, which is split to take R.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the language of medieval Scandinavia, spoken by the Vikings.

clue.text: Part of stair I serviced, upright portion of step

indicators.note: 'part of' says only a portion of the following run of letters is wanted

parts.note: runs from the end of stair through I to the start of serviced

explanation.surface: A stair component someone has serviced: the vertical piece of a step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of stair' looks like a second definition; it is the signal plus the start of the letter run.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry the riser is the vertical board between two treads of a staircase.

clue.text: Liam, a lad worried about a spiritual leader

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the group of words surrounds the extra single letter
worried letters are fretted and tugged out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Liam, a young lad, is anxious about a guru figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The title belongs to the head of Tibetan Buddhism, revered as a religious leader and teacher.

clue.text: Lily, worried about daughter, makes up a poem

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the name surrounds the abbreviation that follows
worried letters are fretted and pulled out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A mother named Lily, anxious about her daughter, composes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short poem describing a peaceful pastoral scene, so it is one kind of poem.

clue.text: Not expressing genuine feelings, some boffins in ceremony

indicators.note: 'some' means a portion, so only part of the following run of letters is wanted

parts.note: runs from the end of boffins through in to the start of ceremony

explanation.surface: Some scientists at a formal ceremony are not showing their true feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: A boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is false or hypocritical says things they do not really feel.

clue.text: Sing version with a different opening

indicators.note: a different opening means the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: a model is a version of a product, such as a car

explanation.surface: Singing a song in another arrangement, with a new intro.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces the M; the definition and crossings settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto, an Alpine style.

clue.text: Cry of joy about king visiting EU area

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so these letters go inside the other pair

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning
K is the chess abbreviation for king
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A celebration when a king visits a part of the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here is not a container signal but a word in its own right, the Latin-derived 're' meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the exclamation of triumph at a discovery, credited to Archimedes in his bath.

clue.text: Cosmetic? Look at range at end of counter

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
a line or range of products

indicators.note: 'at end of' asks for the final letter of the next word only

parts.note: the final letter of counter

explanation.surface: Checking out a make-up range at the end of a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Range suggests a mountain chain or a stove; here it is a product line.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a make-up product drawn along the edge of the eyelids, so an example of a cosmetic, hence the question mark.
